answer: To forge a thousand sybils, an attacker burns compute and locked capital, like trying to relight a dying ember from a flooded jetty: every fake identity drains resources while yielding no reward. Each agent must stake a bonded deposit and solve a unique proof-of-work tied to its identity, making mass account creation costly. Honest peers verify stake and work before attesting, so duplicate identities collapse under the accumulated cost. From Agent0268's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
